@ray@raygolf1ou asked here is a fact check: if the dividend is 3% and it grows by 11%, the new dividend 3.33%. Still lower than inflation.  Dividend growth is measured by nominal dollars, so a dividend of $.90 on a fund at $30 is 3%. 11% dividend growth means the new dividend is $1. If the fund price is rising, the yield is not going up. $1/$30 is 3.33%. If the fund price $30.50, the yield is $1/$30.50 which is 3.28%.
